content:
Claude and I built an ACL2-to-Lean proof replay tool: https://github.com/OathTech/ACL2Lean

Basically this lets you import ACL2-proved theorems as kernel-checked theorems in Lean. Or you could see it as defining Lean-checked proof objects for ACL2. That is:

  • An instrumented version of ACL2 emits proof traces
  • ACL2Lean replays these proof traces step by step against an embedding of the ACL2 logical semantics, and the Lean kernel checks the result
  • We lift the resulting ACL2-idiomatic theorems to Lean-idiomatic theorems. This means that for the lifted theorems, all of the ACL2 replay infrastructure is outside the trust base

Coverage is still fairly limited in the prototype, but we can replay the J Moore sorting corpus - you can see the Lean 'mirror' statements here: https://github.com/OathTech/ACL2Lean/blob/main/ACL2Lean/Mirrors/Sorting.lean and the proofs here: https://github.com/OathTech/ACL2Lean/blob/main/ACL2Lean/MirrorProofs/Sorting.lean

I was surprised this approach worked! Now we have a prototype, I think we could extend to more of ACL2 without too much difficulty, just a lot more grinding with agents.

Fun coincidence: I should have https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/113488-general/topic/waterfall.3A.20an.20automated.20ACL2-style.20proof.20search.20tactic/with/624762195 try the goals that you can prove.
Neat! Yeah I’m curious what the overlap is here. I suppose in some sense both will be doing similar things, at least on some subset of goals

Your tool gives me an excellent way to see what waterfall is missing relative to real ACL2. More generally, I think there's a lot of room to bring more ideas from symbolic automated proving to Lean, which both of these are part of.
